identificationModule.briefTitle: Postoperative Thoracic Epidural Analgesia Versus Intravenous Patient-Controlled Analgesia For Liver and/or Pancreas
identificationModule.officialTitle: Randomized Controlled Trial of Postoperative Thoracic Epidural Analgesia Versus Intravenous Patient Controlled Analgesia (3:1) in Patients Undergoing Liver and/or Pancreatic Resection

armGroups.label: IV Pain Management
armGroups.description: Intravenous analgesia delivered prior to surgery, then patient-controlled following surgical procedures. Hourly post surgery rating level of pain on a scale of 0-10. Questions measure how quickly participant recovers from sedation Day 1 through Day 5 after surgery; approximately 20-40 minutes.

armGroups.label: Epidural Pain Management
armGroups.description: Thoracic epidurals placed preoperatively in either holding area or in operating room. Hourly post surgery rating level of pain on a scale of 0-10. Questions measure how quickly participant recovers from sedation Day 1 through Day 5 after surgery; approximately 20-40 minutes.

interventions.name: Intravenous Patient-Controlled Analgesia (IVPCA)
interventions.description: Intravenous analgesia delivered prior to surgery, then patient-controlled following surgical procedures.

interventions.name: Thoracic Epidural Analgesia (TEA)
interventions.description: Thoracic epidurals (needle inserted into the space between the covering of spinal cord and the cord itself) placed preoperatively in either the holding area or in the operating room.

interventions.name: Questionnaires
interventions.description: Questions measure how quickly participant recovers from sedation Day 1 through Day 5 after surgery; approximately 20-40 minutes.

interventions.name: Pain Assessment
interventions.description: Hourly post surgery rating level of pain on a scale of 0-10.
